title: The desk gadget that was worth more than a salary
hookText:
The most powerful object
on a 1980s desk
caption: The Rolodex was the 1980s' most powerful office object. Here's what it really held.

lines.text: In the 1980s... the most powerful object on a desk wasn't the phone.
It was this. The Rolodex. A little wheel of business cards.
It was invented in 1956 as a simple office tool. Cards on a wheel, A to Z... so a secretary could find a number fast.
Then Hollywood put one on the desk of every powerful character. And people believed it: a fat Rolodex meant you knew everyone.
Because every card was a person. A client. A favour. A deal waiting to happen. Your Rolodex was your network. And your network... was your value.
Then the cards moved into phones. The numbers survived. But the story behind each one... where you met, what they needed... mostly got lost.
Today, you meet more people than ever. And by Friday... you've forgotten who half of them were.
The Rolodex never died. It just needed somewhere to remember.

scenes.picture: Close-up: two hands fight over a Rolodex in a tug of war while cards fly out. Hook text on screen.
scenes.motion: tug of war, cards bursting out, clack at the end

scenes.picture: Camera pulls back from the Rolodex to reveal a 1980s executive behind a huge desk, sunset skyline behind him.
scenes.motion: zoom-in-then-pull-back reveal; rays behind the Rolodex; ROLODEX strip pops

scenes.picture: 1956 office: a secretary next to a Rolodex on a small desk; a card flips A to Z.
scenes.motion: 1956 stamp slams in; A-Z card flip

scenes.picture: A stage with curtains; a film reel spins; a TV shows a powerful man whose Rolodex grows bigger.
scenes.motion: TV rises, mini Rolodex grows with rays and sparkles

scenes.picture: Cards fly out of the Rolodex and become six little people connected by strings; then wind blows them away and a phone rises; paper notes fly away.
scenes.motion: cards turn into people; strings; wind; phone rises; notes blow away

scenes.picture: Trade-show hall; a confused young visitor; question marks pop.
scenes.motion: visitor slides in, sways; ? tiles pop on 'forgotten'

scenes.picture: A business card is scanned into a phone and becomes a contact with a note 'Met at GITEX'. Small logo.
scenes.motion: scan beam, note chip pops, logo fades in

factNotes: Invented in 1956; the inventor is disputed, so the script names no one. Sources: Wikipedia (Rolodex); Cooper Hewitt, 'The power of the Rolodex' (2014).
